target_customer: SaaS and AI companies that need product integrations with customers' other software
problem: Building and maintaining OAuth and API integrations for each third party tool takes engineering months.
business_model: Open source with hosted cloud, usage-based pricing
product_category: Integration infrastructure (auth, syncs, unified API, MCP tools)

founders.name: Robin Guldener
previous_startups: Avrios (co-founder, fleet management SaaS, over 1,000 customers)

founders.name: Bastien Beurier
previous_startups: Two earlier YC startups (names not stated on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Self described recidivist founder (2 x YC).

technical_complexity.rationale: Many provider specific OAuth and API quirks across hundreds of APIs, standard engineering at volume.

defensibility.rationale: Open source community and a growing catalog of integrations create stickiness, though code can be forked.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors listed in 2026 comparison blogs remain independent; no incumbent absorbed the wedge in sources found.

market_need_then: Founders cite experience of how hard SaaS integrations are to build; the product began as an open source OAuth handler for 40 APIs.

branding.brand_signature: Open source repo (13.2k GitHub stars per site) and community Slack
branding.community_and_virality: Public GitHub project with community Slack and a published brand guideline page.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong open source following for a dev tool, but no press about the brand itself.

pivots.to: Unified API, then integrations platform for AI agents
pivots.why: Company About page says it relaunched as a unified API after the W23 batch; later repositioned for agents. Dates not stated.

outcome_analysis: Nango grew from an open source OAuth tool into an integrations platform with named customers such as Replit and a reported cash flow positive state when it raised a 7.5M seed in April 2026. Growth was bootstrapped on a small convertible raise, which points to capital efficiency, and the 2026 round is its first verified one.
notes: The blog post says Nango was founded in 2023 while YC says 2022. CB Insights lists a 500K convertible note on 2023-01-01 (aggregator only, not recorded). Other total-raised figures vary by aggregator. Competition near 2023 not found in dated sources (results were 2026 comparison blogs), so list is empty. Company claims cash flow positive per its own post.
